description: Phase 8 example inventory (issues #13, #14): every example the book prints, one entry each. Checked by tests/regression/example-inventory.test.ts through tests/support/example-inventory.ts. Each entry gives section_id, pdf_page and printed_page (from corpus/source-map/pages.yaml, never computed), a short verbatim anchor, a form (labelled_example: the three nodes labelled example; inline_prose; caption; table; diagram) and one disposition with a non-empty reason. executable: the printed outcome is checked by the source_example cases listed in order in cases. descriptive: the example has no checkable outcome, and the reason says why. source_conflicted: the printed result disagrees with the rules; issues names the review/ issues, and any cases keep the printed values. missing_information: the example needs something the book does not give (a not_present book, a card, an unprinted value); the reason names it. Every source_example case is claimed by exactly one entry. Until #20, an executable entry not yet converted carries pending: true and no cases, and unswept_sections lists the sections not yet searched for examples; the chapter slices (#15-#19) remove the sections they sweep.

entries.anchor: For example, the Doors Rule can easily be placed by the piles of Exploration Cards to expedite the handling of doors and traps.
entries.reason: Illustrates how a Rule Card is used at the table (placed by the Exploration Card piles); it gives no roll, value or outcome. The door rules it points to have their own cases.

entries.anchor: Sometimes you will be asked to add a modifier to the roll (for instance +10).
entries.reason: Names a sample modifier (+10) without a skill level, roll or result, so there is no outcome to check; modified checks are covered by the core.check cases.

entries.anchor: Throughout these rules you will find examples of that.
entries.reason: Points to the photographs of other tiles and 3D terrain printed throughout the book; they illustrate presentation only and carry no rule outcome.

entries.anchor: All 8 squares within the green square are adjacent to the blue square
entries.reason: The caption fixes which of the eight surrounding squares are adjacent; one case per square.

entries.anchor: If you are searching for hidden secrets in a room, you will be required to face a Perception Test.
entries.reason: Names which check a situation calls for (Perception Test to search, Strength Check to force a portcullis) with no roll, value or outcome; the procedures that run those checks carry their own cases.

entries.anchor: For example: ‘If adjacent, then….
entries.reason: Quotes the kind of rule wording that uses "adjacent"; the condition is left unfinished, so there is nothing to check. The adjacency definition itself is checked by example.game_basics.adjacent_squares.

entries.anchor: a model with the Large Special Rule (such as a Troll) should be large enough to occupy 4 squares
entries.reason: Whether a Troll has the Large Special Rule is monster data in the Bestiary, which is not_present; this PDF gives no Troll profile to check the example against.

entries.anchor: A character in square A would not have LOS to a character in square B
entries.reason: The diagram gives three sight lines from A with printed results: blocked by the tile border, obstructed by the fountain, and clear.

entries.anchor: The players roll the Scenario die, 1d10, and get a 2.
entries.reason: Multi-step worked example (PDF 22-24) run as ordered source_example cases with the printed rolls pinned. Steps that disagree with the rules keep their printed values and are not executed as the adjusted value: the Threat values (chest_threat), the trap Sanity loss of 1 against the table's -2 (trap_sanity), the Legendary Items column and die (legendary_roll), the spider turn (spider_turn), the in-battle Threat result (threat_table_result) and the torch bonus after the Threat Roll (torch_after_threat_roll). The spider initiative step follows changelog 2.21 entry 27. The trap step depends on trap cards, which are not in this PDF. Not executed for missing information: the spider's bite (its Combat Skill), its 19 remaining Hit Points and its fear level are Bestiary data (not_present), the Fear Tests print no rolls or Resolve values, and the 2d6 placement prints no rolls.

entries.anchor: A class 3 weapon would require a minimum strength of 30 to use with two hands
entries.reason: Printed STR thresholds for class 3 in two and one hands, and the two-hand limits of classes 5 and 6.

entries.anchor: A Warrior has a -20 modifier to Pick Locks.
entries.reason: Printed arithmetic: the Free skill bonus turns -20 into -10.

entries.anchor: Wilbur’s RES is 37.
entries.reason: Printed arithmetic: RES 37 contributes 3 to Party Morale.

entries.anchor: I would like to make a new character.
entries.reason: Multi-step worked example (PDF 49-50) run as ordered source_example cases in printed order. Its skills sheet, coin total and prayer bonus disagree with the catalogues, and the background roll names no die; the issues record these and the cases keep the printed values.

entries.anchor: A Class 3 weapon requires a minimum strength of 30 to use with two hands
entries.reason: Printed STR thresholds for class 3 in two and one hands, and the two-hand limit of class 5.

entries.anchor: if you have two active conditions, your maximum Sanity is now 6
entries.reason: Printed value: two active conditions lower maximum Sanity to 6.

entries.anchor: if two heroes are poisoned, you suffer a -2 modifier
entries.reason: Printed value: two poisoned heroes give a -2 Party Morale modifier.

entries.anchor: A warrior has CS 80.
entries.reason: Printed outcomes: CS 80 cannot be raised at level up (natural maximum 80); CS 80 +10 +20 gives 110; and a roll in the printed 91-00 range still misses (cases pin both ends of that range).

entries.anchor: it is easier for a barbarian to master combat skills, and a thief will be more adept at learning to pick locks
entries.reason: A qualitative comparison of professions with no printed cost or outcome; "combat skills" is not tied to a named row, and the costs themselves are table.character.improvement_costs data.

entries.anchor: The Level 4 Wizard, Ozmor, has decided to cast the ‘Summon Demon Spell’
entries.reason: Run as a source_example case with the printed rolls. Its miscast threshold and Mana cost disagree with the Focus rule and the spell catalogue; the issue records both and the case keeps the printed values.

entries.anchor: A Magic Bolt Spell requires the caster to be Level 3
entries.reason: Printed arithmetic: a scroll lowers Magic Bolt CV 10 to 0, so Arcane Arts 50 succeeds on 50 or lower.

entries.anchor: drinking 2 potions of dexterity does not give you double the effect
entries.reason: Printed outcomes: two dexterity potions do not stack; one strength and one dexterity potion both apply.

entries.anchor: Both upper placements work.
entries.reason: The caption gives the printed verdict for each tile placement in the figure.

entries.anchor: For example, 4 Room Cards and 4 Corridor Cards.
entries.reason: Printed outcome: eight cards put the Objective Room at least 4 tiles deep.

entries.anchor: At the start of the turn, the player rolls the Scenario die, 1d10. It ends up a 9
entries.reason: Printed rolls and results (PDF 89-90): Scenario die 9 demands a Threat roll, 7 against Threat 9 triggers the table and drops the level by 6, and the counterfactual roll above 9 raises it to 10.

entries.anchor: A character in square A could move to square 1 since the diagonal movement is between two friends.
entries.reason: The diagram gives a printed verdict for each move from A: squares 1 to 4 and the blocked straight moves.

entries.anchor: Moving from A to B is not allowed as it touches the black outline of the tile.
entries.reason: The diagram gives a printed verdict: a diagonal move along the tile border is not allowed.

entries.anchor: In the example to the right, that means that only the white square is blocked
entries.reason: The diagram gives the printed verdict for the torture rack: only the white square is blocked.

entries.anchor: Belleck spends 1 AP examining a fallen enemy and finds a leather cap
entries.reason: Printed outcome: swapping the caps costs no AP beyond the search.

entries.anchor: A hero with DB 1 is pushing an enemy with DEX 35.
entries.reason: Printed arithmetic: DB 1 adds 10, so 26 and up succeeds against DEX 35.

entries.anchor: In the lower example, the Wizard shoves the Gnoll.
entries.reason: The caption gives printed outcomes for both figures: the diagonal push, the Gnoll at the back stepping back, and the fall when it cannot.

entries.anchor: Characters A, B and C are all armed with ranged weapons and try to fire at E.
entries.reason: The diagram gives printed results for each shooter: A cannot fire, B at -10, C at -20, and B hitting D on 90 or more.

entries.anchor: Here, the enemy is adjacent to a hero.
entries.reason: Italic explanation the book prints "specifically for this example": the adjacent enemy makes room once, then attacks.

entries.anchor: If you roll Parry in the first action, treat that as the second action
entries.reason: Italic explanation for option 2: Parry rolled on the first action becomes a Standard Attack, then Parry Stance.

entries.anchor: In this case, the enemy is close enough to reach a hero with one move.
entries.reason: Italic explanation for option 3: a Parry Stance result on the first action means the enemy does not move. Only the derived case test.combat.humanoid_behaviour.approach_parry models it; the Combat slice (#16) converts it.

entries.anchor: That is, if the enemy is further away than it can move
entries.reason: Italic explanation for option 4: an enemy out of reach walks towards the closest hero.

entries.anchor: Berthram manages to parry an incoming strike causing 8 Points of Damage.
entries.reason: Printed arithmetic: shield DEF 6 leaves 2 damage, the shield takes 1, and the padded jacket absorbs the rest.

entries.anchor: Round 1. Variya the Barbarian is facing two ferocious Gnolls.
entries.reason: Multi-step worked example run as ordered source_example cases with the printed rolls pinned. Its Gnoll behaviour rolls, Frenzy AP and wounded label disagree with the rules; the issue records each and the cases keep the printed values.

entries.anchor: Blue arrows would cost 5 points of movement and would require a horse.
entries.reason: The caption gives printed movement costs for the blue and green routes.

entries.anchor: The party is in Irondale and has decided to take on the quest
entries.reason: Printed roll and result: 1d6 gives 1, read in turquoise for Irondale.

entries.anchor: This party has just arrived at the settlement (Silver City in this case)
entries.reason: The printed day-by-day table gives each hero’s activities; the case checks the Wizard learning a spell over D1-D3 and the party leaving on D4.

entries.anchor: Quest 1 dictates a Wandering Monster appears when the Threat Level reaches 12.
entries.reason: Printed outcomes: reaching 12 places a monster, falling back to 12 does not, and rising to 12 again does.
